content: 1. Nevirapine is metabolized by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor patients when co-administering drugs that interact with this enzyme. 2. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce systemic exposure to flibanserin. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Fluconazole increases nevirapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 4. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Nevirapine reduces the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fosamprenavir and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor. 6. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Fosphenytoin reduces the levels or effects of nevirapine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer, increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily. Resume the standard dose of 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the strong inducer. 9. Nevirapine reduces the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, potentially leading to a loss of therapeutic effect. Use caution and monitor. 10. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of guanfacine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce guanfacine plasma concentrations and elimination half-life. If co-administered, more frequent dosing of the immediate-release (IR) product may be required to achieve or maintain the desired hypotensive response. For patients with ADHD, the FDA-approved labeling for extended-release (ER) guanfacine recommends considering doubling the dose if co-administered with a CYP3A4 inducer. 11. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Exercise caution when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone, as plasma concentrations of hydrocodone may increase, potentially resulting in fatal respiratory depression. 12. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Nevirapine increases the effects of ifosfamide by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP2B6 inducers may increase the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active metabolite. Nevirapine also increases the toxicity of ifosfamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to the formation of neurotoxic and nephrotoxic metabolites such as chloroacetaldehyde. Closely monitor patients for toxicities and consider dose adjustments. 15. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone increases nevirapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 16. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both indinavir and nevirapine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Indinavir increases nevirapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Istradefylline increases nevirapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. In clinical trials, istradefylline 40 mg/day increased the peak levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 19. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ixabepilone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ketamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
